title: Javonte Pays Off in Pillbert Debut, Zoe Snaps the Commish's Streak, and Four Teams Share First
dek: Two big underdogs cashed in Week 4, HULK and The Horse is Hea both lost, and the standings now have a four-way tie at the top.
body: The trade everyone circled delivered right away. Alan's Team Pillbert beat Ramon's No Banner only HULK 125.42 to 116.72 as a 29% underdog, and the difference-maker was the guy Philly got from Randy a week ago: Javonte Williams posted 28.8 points on a 13.25 projection in his first start in Pillbert colors. Alan won by 8.7 while Kyle Monangai scored 27.5 on his bench, so this could have been a rout. His title odds more than doubled, from 9% to 21%, and Team Pillbert is riding the league's only three-game winning streak. The bad guy didn't just survive the juggernaut, he looked like he had a plan for it.

HULK wasn't bad, it was just beaten. Kenneth Walker III went for 30.4 on an 18.89 projection, and Ramon still leads the league with 561 points, 80.1 more than anyone else. The new arrival didn't factor in: Rashee Rice scored zero and didn't start in his HULK debut. Brucie's title odds sit at 41%, still the best in the league by nearly 20 points, and he spent the week tinkering, grabbing Jason Myers right after Alan cut him, swapping Cameron Dicker out, and adding the Bills D/ST. A Chicago kid rostering Buffalo's defense on purpose is a choice, but at least it's an honest one.

The other upset belonged to the rookie. Zoe's Ghostu-Spider SZN beat Sonny's The Horse is Hea 120.88 to 95.1 as a 30% underdog, behind Tetairoa McMillan's 38.2 on a 13.5 projection, the best individual week in the league, plus 27.2 from Bijan Robinson. Zilgit even left Nico Collins and his 27.3 on the bench and still won by almost 26. She also swapped Kyler Murray for Jared Goff, and at 2-2 she's back to .500 with a winning streak of her own. A month into her first season, she's already beating commissioners.

Sonny's afternoon was the opposite of last week's. Parker Washington posted 1.5 points on a 12.79 projection, and Chuba Hubbard, the back he traded for, scored 25.4 from the bench. Even if you dropped those 23.9 extra points into the lineup, The Horse is Hea still comes up 1.88 short, which is the only consolation the commish gets. His title odds now read 11%, and he went shopping hard: Tony Pollard for J.K. Dobbins, Juwan Johnson, Bryce Young off Alan's scrap heap, Mark Andrews out the door, and the Bears D/ST in for the Eagles. The Boston transplant still knows which defense to trust when it matters, apparently.

Kaushal finally got his first win, and he made it loud. Habibsters put up 140.1, the week's top score, in a 43-point thumping of Randy's The fumblers, who were 61% favorites. CeeDee Lamb went for 32.8 on a 13.65 projection, and the two-time champ now has 459.1 points, more than 3-1 Randy's 458.7. Habib's title odds jumped from 1% to 8%, and he kept the wire spinning with Sam Darnold for Drake Maye, Braelon Allen for Kyle Pitts Sr., Keenan Allen, and the Vikings D/ST. For Randy, the trade review is not flattering: Stefon Diggs gave him 6 points while Javonte was busy beating HULK. He responded by adding Trevor Lawrence and dropping Justin Herbert, plus Darren Waller for Hunter Henry and Jordan Addison.

Mekhi got off the mat too. Dawgs beat Jordan's Counting or not Counting GV 107.54 to 90.22, with Kyren Williams posting 31.7 on an 11.88 projection, and Kai won despite Ja'Marr Chase managing 4.2 on a 16.54 projection, the week's biggest bust. JMoney had his own receiver problem, with Garrett Wilson also stuck at 4.2, and he falls to 0-4 with 349.2 points and 0% playoff odds. He reshuffled with Kirk Cousins for Marvin Harrison Jr., Dalton Schultz for Michael Pittman Jr., and Michael Wilson for Tank Bigsby. The numbers guy is now staring at the one number he can't spin.

The trade ledger also shows Philly working the phones beyond the Javonte deal. Alan sent Isaiah Likely, Emeka Egbuka, and Denzel Boston to Jordan for Ashton Jeanty, and Jeanty ended up with Mekhi along with Davante Adams in a deal that brought Justin Jefferson to Team Pillbert. Add the Achane drop, plus Ollie Gordon II, Tyreek Hill, Kalif Raymond, and kicker Spencer Shrader, and Alan is rebuilding a 3-1 team in real time. Bold for a contender, but the model just rewarded him for it.

The standings: No Banner only HULK, Team Pillbert, The Horse is Hea, and The fumblers are all 3-1, with Ghostu-Spider SZN at 2-2, Habibsters and Dawgs at 1-3, and Counting or not Counting GV at 0-4. Week 5's best game is Dawgs against Team Pillbert, a straight-up revenge setup with Adams and Jeanty facing the team that sent them away and Jefferson facing his old manager. HULK and The fumblers meet in a battle of 3-1 teams, Habib tries to keep climbing against the commish, and Zoe gets a chance to push JMoney to 0-5. Four teams share first place, and by Sunday night at least two of them won't.

social.author: Pillbert Partisans
social.text: 29% to win. Javonte drops 28.8 in his debut. HULK goes down. Title odds 9% to 21%. Thank you, Randy. Sincerely.

social.author: Web Slingers Fan Club
social.text: McMillan 38.2. Bijan 27.2. Nico Collins benched and we STILL won by 26. Rookie season? Sure. Rookie mistakes? Not today.

social.author: Neigh Sayers Anonymous
social.text: Hubbard on the bench: 25.4. Parker Washington in the lineup: 1.5. We do not wish to discuss the lineup screen at this time.

social.author: Buckaroo Analytics Dept.
social.text: Habibsters: 1-3, 459.1 points. The fumblers: 3-1, 458.7 points. Football is a cruel and beautiful sport.

social.author: Dawg Pound Dispatch
social.text: Chase gives us 4.2 and we win anyway. Kyren 31.7. Now Adams and Jeanty get Philly next week. Mark your calendars.

social.author: Fumbler Fan 1985
social.text: Diggs: 6 points. Javonte: 28.8 against HULK. I'm not saying we want a refund. I'm saying where's the receipt.

social.author: HULK Smash Society
social.text: One loss. Still 561 points. Still 41%. Still the team you have to go through. Fumblers, you're next.

social.author: Buckaroo Insider
social.text: Sources say Philly's front office has made more transactions this month than some teams made all of 2025. Jefferson is the latest piece.

social.author: Habib Hive
social.text: 140.1. Top score of the week. Two rings, one W, and the odds just went from 1% to 8%. Told you not to bury the champ.

trade_watch.take: The paper verdict just became a scoreboard verdict: Javonte put up 28.8 in his Pillbert debut and keyed the upset of HULK, while Diggs gave Randy 6 in a 43-point loss. Philly was already winning this deal on paper, and now it's a landslide.

Week 1 of the Chuba-for-Rice era: Hubbard scored 25.4 on Sonny's bench, Rice scored zero and didn't start for Ramon. Both teams lost, so for now this deal is a tie at zero useful lineup points apiece, with Sonny holding the player who's actually producing.

bios.1: Sonny's perfect start ended against Zoe, with Chuba Hubbard's 25.4 stranded on the bench and Parker Washington posting 1.5. At 3-1 with 11% title odds, the commish is reshuffling hard with Tony Pollard, Juwan Johnson, and the Bears D/ST.
bios.2: Randy's team got run over by Kaushal 140.1 to 96.88, and Stefon Diggs has given him 6 points since the trade. Still 3-1 with 72% playoff odds, but swapping Justin Herbert for Trevor Lawrence and facing HULK next week raises the stakes.
bios.3: Jordan is 0-4 with a league-low 349.2 points and 0% playoff odds after Garrett Wilson managed 4.2. Kirk Cousins, Dalton Schultz, and the pieces from the Jeanty deal are the building blocks for whatever comes next.
bios.4: Alan has won three straight, took down HULK as a big underdog, and saw his title odds jump to 21%. Javonte Williams is paying off, Justin Jefferson is on the way in, and Philly keeps rebuilding a contender on the fly.
bios.5: Mekhi got his first win behind Kyren Williams' 31.7 even with Ja'Marr Chase stuck at 4.2. Now Davante Adams and Ashton Jeanty join the Dawgs, just in time for a date with the team that traded them away.
bios.6: Kaushal finally won, posting the week's top score and climbing from 1% to 8% title odds. At 1-3 with more points than 3-1 Randy, the two-time champ has a real case that his record is lying.
bios.7: Ramon's juggernaut finally lost, falling to Alan as a 71% favorite, but it still leads the league with 561 points and 41% title odds. Rashee Rice hasn't contributed yet, and a 3-1 showdown with Randy comes next.
bios.8: Zoe upset the commissioner behind Tetairoa McMillan's league-best 38.2 and is back to 2-2. She's still a long shot at 2% title odds, but the rookie is making moves like a veteran, Jared Goff included.
